title: Poems (First Series et al.)
author: Emily Dickinson
note: Poems (First Series et al.) — a full sitting.

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: Success is counted sweetest By those who ne'er succeed.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: Our share of night to bear, Our share of morning, Our blank in bliss to fill, Our blank in scorning.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: Soul, wilt thou toss again?

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: T is so much joy! 'T is so much joy!

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: Glee! The great storm is over!

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: If I can stop one heart from breaking, I shall not live in vain; If I can ease one life the aching, Or cool one pain, Or help one fainting robin Unto his nest again, I shall not live in vain.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: ALMOST! Within my reach!

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: A wounded deer leaps highest, I've heard the hunter tell; 'T is but the ecstasy of death, And then the brake is still.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: The heart asks pleasure first, And then, excuse from pain; And then, those little anodynes That deaden suffering; And then, to go to sleep; And then, if it should be The will of its Inquisitor, The liberty to die.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: A precious, mouldering pleasure 't is To meet an antique book, In just the dress his century wore; A privilege, I think, His venerable hand to take, And warming in our own, A passage back, or two, to make To times when he was young.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: Much madness is divinest sense To a discerning eye; Much sense the starkest madness. 'T is the majority In this, as all, prevails.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: I asked no other thing, No other was denied.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: The soul selects her own society, Then shuts the door; On her divine majority Obtrude no more.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: Some things that fly there be, -Birds, hours, the bumble-bee: Of these no elegy.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: I know some lonely houses off the road A robber 'd like the look of, -Wooden barred, And windows hanging low, Inviting to A portico, Where two could creep: One hand the tools, The other peep To make sure all's asleep.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: To fight aloud is very brave, But gallanter, I know, Who charge within the bosom, The cavalry of woe.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: DAWN. When night is almost done, And sunrise grows so near That we can touch the spaces, It 's time to smooth the hair And get the dimples ready, And wonder we could care For that old faded midnight That frightened but an hour.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: Read, sweet, how others strove, Till we are stouter; What they renounced, Till we are less afraid; How many times they bore The faithful witness, Till we are helped, As if a kingdom cared!

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: Pain has an element of blank; It cannot recollect When it began, or if there were A day when it was not.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: I taste a liquor never brewed, From tankards scooped in pearl; Not all the vats upon the Rhine Yield such an alcohol!

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: A BOOK. He ate and drank the precious words, His spirit grew robust; He knew no more that he was poor, Nor that his frame was dust.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: I had no time to hate, because The grave would hinder me, And life was not so ample I Could finish enmity.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: T was such a little, little boat That toddled down the bay! 'T was such a gallant, gallant sea That beckoned it away! ' T was such a greedy, greedy wave That licked it from the coast; Nor ever guessed the stately sails My little craft was lost!

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: Whether my bark went down at sea, Whether she met with gales, Whether to isles enchanted She bent her docile sails; By what mystic mooring She is held to-day, -This is the errand of the eye Out upon the bay.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: Belshazzar had a letter, -He never had but one; Belshazzar's correspondent Concluded and begun In that immortal copy The conscience of us all Can read without its glasses On revelation's wall.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: The brain within its groove Runs evenly and true; But let a splinter swerve, 'T were easier for you To put the water back When floods have slit the hills, And scooped a turnpike for themselves, And blotted out the mills!

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: MINE. Mine by the right of the white election!

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: BEQUEST.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: Alter? When the hills do.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: Elysium is as far as to The very nearest room, If in that room a friend await Felicity or doom.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: Doubt me, my dim companion!

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: If you were coming in the fall, I'd brush the summer by With half a smile and half a spurn, As housewives do a fly.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: I hide myself within my flower, That wearing on your breast, You, unsuspecting, wear me too -And angels know the rest.

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: PROOF. That I did always love, I bring thee proof: That till I loved I did not love enough.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: Have you got a brook in your little heart, Where bashful flowers blow, And blushing birds go down to drink, And shadows tremble so?

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: As if some little Arctic flower, Upon the polar hem, Went wandering down the latitudes, Until it puzzled came To continents of summer, To firmaments of sun, To strange, bright crowds of flowers, And birds of foreign tongue!

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: My river runs to thee: Blue sea, wilt welcome me?

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: IN VAIN.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: There came a day at summer's full Entirely for me; I thought that such were for the saints, Where revelations be.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: I'm ceded, I've stopped being theirs; The name they dropped upon my face With water, in the country church, Is finished using now, And they can put it with my dolls, My childhood, and the string of spools I've finished threading too.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: T was a long parting, but the time For interview had come; Before the judgment-seat of God, The last and second time These fleshless lovers met, A heaven in a gaze, A heaven of heavens, the privilege Of one another's eyes.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: I'm wife; I've finished that, That other state; I'm Czar, I'm woman now: It's safer so.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: THE WIFE.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: Come slowly, Eden!

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: New feet within my garden go, New fingers stir the sod; A troubadour upon the elm Betrays the solitude.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: Pink, small, and punctual, Aromatic, low, Covert in April, Candid in May, Dear to the moss, Known by the knoll, Next to the robin In every human soul.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: WHY? The murmur of a bee A witchcraft yieldeth me.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: Perhaps you'd like to buy a flower?

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: The pedigree of honey Does not concern the bee; A clover, any time, to him Is aristocracy.

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: Some keep the Sabbath going to church; I keep it staying at home, With a bobolink for a chorister, And an orchard for a dome.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: The bee is not afraid of me, I know the butterfly; The pretty people in the woods Receive me cordially.

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: Some rainbow coming from the fair!

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: The grass so little has to do, -A sphere of simple green, With only butterflies to brood, And bees to entertain, And stir all day to pretty tunes The breezes fetch along, And hold the sunshine in its lap And bow to everything; And thread the dews all night, like pearls, And make itself so fine, -A duchess were too common For such a noticing.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: A little road not made of man, Enabled of the eye, Accessible to thill of bee, Or cart of butterfly.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: A drop fell on the apple tree, Another on the roof; A half a dozen kissed the eaves, And made the gables laugh.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: A something in a summer's day, As slow her flambeaux burn away, Which solemnizes me.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: This is the land the sunset washes, These are the banks of the Yellow Sea; Where it rose, or whither it rushes, These are the western mystery!

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: There is a flower that bees prefer, And butterflies desire; To gain the purple democrat The humming-birds aspire.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: THE BEE.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: Presentiment is that long shadow on the lawn Indicative that suns go down; The notice to the startled grass That darkness is about to pass.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: As children bid the guest good-night, And then reluctant turn, My flowers raise their pretty lips, Then put their nightgowns on.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: Angels in the early morning May be seen the dews among, Stooping, plucking, smiling, flying: Do the buds to them belong?

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: So bashful when I spied her, So pretty, so ashamed!

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: It makes no difference abroad, The seasons fit the same, The mornings blossom into noons, And split their pods of flame.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: The mountain sat upon the plain In his eternal chair, His observation omnifold, His inquest everywhere.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: A DAY. I'll tell you how the sun rose, -A ribbon at a time.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: The butterfly's assumption-gown, In chrysoprase apartments hung, This afternoon put on.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: THE WIND.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: Apparently with no surprise To any happy flower, The frost beheads it at its play In accidental power.

scenes.title: XXVI. '
scenes.reentry: T WAS later when the summer went Than when the cricket came, And yet we knew that gentle clock Meant nought but going home. ' T was sooner when the cricket went Than when the winter came, Yet that pathetic pendulum Keeps esoteric time.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: These are the days when birds come back, A very few, a bird or two, To take a backward look.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: AUTUMN. The morns are meeker than they were, The nuts are getting brown; The berry's cheek is plumper, The rose is out of town.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: The sky is low, the clouds are mean, A travelling flake of snow Across a barn or through a rut Debates if it will go.

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: I think the hemlock likes to stand Upon a marge of snow; It suits his own austerity, And satisfies an awe That men must slake in wilderness, Or in the desert cloy, -An instinct for the hoar, the bald, Lapland's necessity.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: There's a certain slant of light, On winter afternoons, That oppresses, like the weight Of cathedral tunes.

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: One dignity delays for all, One mitred afternoon.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: TOO LATE.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: Departed to the judgment, A mighty afternoon; Great clouds like ushers leaning, Creation looking on.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: Safe in their alabaster chambers, Untouched by morning and untouched by noon, Sleep the meek members of the resurrection, Rafter of satin, and roof of stone.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: On this long storm the rainbow rose, On this late morn the sun; The clouds, like listless elephants, Horizons straggled down.

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: My cocoon tightens, colors tease, I'm feeling for the air; A dim capacity for wings Degrades the dress I wear.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: Exultation is the going Of an inland soul to sea, -Past the houses, past the headlands, Into deep eternity!

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: Look back on time with kindly eyes, He doubtless did his best; How softly sinks his trembling sun In human nature's west!

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: A train went through a burial gate, A bird broke forth and sang, And trilled, and quivered, and shook his throat Till all the churchyard rang; And then adjusted his little notes, And bowed and sang again.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: I died for beauty, but was scarce Adjusted in the tomb, When one who died for truth was lain In an adjoining room.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: How many times these low feet staggered, Only the soldered mouth can tell; Try! can you stir the awful rivet?

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: REAL. I like a look of agony, Because I know it 's true; Men do not sham convulsion, Nor simulate a throe.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: That short, potential stir That each can make but once, That bustle so illustrious 'T is almost consequence, Is the eclat of death.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: I went to thank her, But she slept; Her bed a funnelled stone, With nosegays at the head and foot, That travellers had thrown, Who went to thank her; But she slept. 'T was short to cross the sea To look upon her like, alive, But turning back 't was slow.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: I've seen a dying eye Run round and round a room In search of something, as it seemed, Then cloudier become; And then, obscure with fog, And then be soldered down, Without disclosing what it be, 'T were blessed to have seen.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: REFUGE. The clouds their backs together laid, The north begun to push, The forests galloped till they fell, The lightning skipped like mice; The thunder crumbled like a stuff -How good to be safe in tombs, Where nature's temper cannot reach, Nor vengeance ever comes!

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: I never saw a moor, I never saw the sea; Yet know I how the heather looks, And what a wave must be.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: God permits industrious angels Afternoons to play.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: To know just how he suffered would be dear; To know if any human eyes were near To whom he could intrust his wavering gaze, Until it settled firm on Paradise.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: The last night that she lived, It was a common night, Except the dying; this to us Made nature different.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: Not in this world to see his face Sounds long, until I read the place Where this is said to be But just the primer to a life Unopened, rare, upon the shelf, Clasped yet to him and me.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: The bustle in a house The morning after death Is solemnest of industries Enacted upon earth, -The sweeping up the heart, And putting love away We shall not want to use again Until eternity.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: I reason, earth is short, And anguish absolute, And many hurt; But what of that?

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: Afraid? Of whom am I afraid?

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: DYING. The sun kept setting, setting still; No hue of afternoon Upon the village I perceived, -From house to house 't was noon.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: Two swimmers wrestled on the spar Until the morning sun, When one turned smiling to the land.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: Because I could not stop for Death, He kindly stopped for me; The carriage held but just ourselves And Immortality.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: She went as quiet as the dew From a familiar flower.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: At last to be identified!

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: Except to heaven, she is nought; Except for angels, lone; Except to some wide-wandering bee, A flower superfluous blown; Except for winds, provincial; Except by butterflies, Unnoticed as a single dew That on the acre lies.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: Death is a dialogue between The spirit and the dust.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXII
scenes.reentry: It was too late for man, But early yet for God; Creation impotent to help, But prayer remained our side.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIII
scenes.reentry: When I was small, a woman died.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIV
scenes.reentry: The daisy follows soft the sun, And when his golden walk is done, Sits shyly at his feet.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXV
scenes.reentry: No rack can torture me, My soul's at liberty Behind this mortal bone There knits a bolder one You cannot prick with saw, Nor rend with scymitar.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVI
scenes.reentry: LOST. I lost a world the other day.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVII
scenes.reentry: If I shouldn't be alive When the robins come, Give the one in red cravat A memorial crumb.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIX
scenes.reentry: I shall know why, when time is over, And I have ceased to wonder why; Christ will explain each separate anguish In the fair schoolroom of the sky.

scenes.title: Chapter XL
scenes.reentry: I never lost as much but twice, And that was in the sod; Twice have I stood a beggar Before the door of God!

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: I'm nobody!

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: I bring an unaccustomed wine To lips long parching, next to mine, And summon them to drink.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: The nearest dream recedes, unrealized.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: We play at paste, Till qualified for pearl, Then drop the paste, And deem ourself a fool.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: I found the phrase to every thought I ever had, but one; And that defies me, -- as a hand Did try to chalk the sun To races nurtured in the dark; -How would your own begin?

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: HOPE. Hope is the thing with feathers That perches in the soul, And sings the tune without the words, And never stops at all, And sweetest in the gale is heard; And sore must be the storm That could abash the little bird That kept so many warm.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: Dare you see a soul at the white heat?

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: Who never lost, are unprepared A coronet to find; Who never thirsted, flagons And cooling tamarind.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: THE TEST.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: ESCAPE. I never hear the word "escape" Without a quicker blood, A sudden expectation, A flying attitude.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: For each ecstatic instant We must an anguish pay In keen and quivering ratio To the ecstasy.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: Through the straight pass of suffering The martyrs even trod, Their feet upon temptation, Their faces upon God.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: A PRAYER.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: The thought beneath so slight a film Is more distinctly seen, -As laces just reveal the surge, Or mists the Apennine.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: The soul unto itself Is an imperial friend, -Or the most agonizing spy An enemy could send.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: Surgeons must be very careful When they take the knife!

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: I like to see it lap the miles, And lick the valleys up, And stop to feed itself at tanks; And then, prodigious, step Around a pile of mountains, And, supercilious, peer In shanties by the sides of roads; And then a quarry pare To fit its sides, and crawl between, Complaining all the while In horrid, hooting stanza; Then chase itself down hill And neigh like Boanerges; Then, punctual as a star, Stop -- docile and omnipotent -At its own stable door.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: THE SHOW.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: Delight becomes pictorial When viewed through pain, -More fair, because impossible That any gain.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: A thought went up my mind to-day That I have had before, But did not finish, -- some way back, I could not fix the year, Nor where it went, nor why it came The second time to me, Nor definitely what it was, Have I the art to say.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: Is Heaven a physician?

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: Though I get home how late, how late!

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: A poor torn heart, a tattered heart, That sat it down to rest, Nor noticed that the ebbing day Flowed silver to the west, Nor noticed night did soft descend Nor constellation burn, Intent upon the vision Of latitudes unknown.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: TOO MUCH.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: It tossed and tossed, -A little brig I knew, -O'ertook by blast, It spun and spun, And groped delirious, for morn.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: Victory comes late, And is held low to freezing lips Too rapt with frost To take it.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: ENOUGH. God gave a loaf to every bird, But just a crumb to me; I dare not eat it, though I starve, -My poignant luxury To own it, touch it, prove the feat That made the pellet mine, -Too happy in my sparrow chance For ampler coveting.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: Experiment to me Is every one I meet.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: My country need not change her gown, Her triple suit as sweet As when 't was cut at Lexington, And first pronounced "a fit."

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: Faith is a fine invention For gentlemen who see; But microscopes are prudent In an emergency!

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: Except the heaven had come so near, So seemed to choose my door, The distance would not haunt me so; I had not hoped before.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXII
scenes.reentry: Portraits are to daily faces As an evening west To a fine, pedantic sunshine In a satin vest.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIII
scenes.reentry: THE DUEL.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIV
scenes.reentry: A shady friend for torrid days Is easier to find Than one of higher temperature For frigid hour of mind.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXV
scenes.reentry: THE GOAL.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVI
scenes.reentry: SIGHT. Before I got my eye put out, I liked as well to see As other creatures that have eyes, And know no other way.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVII
scenes.reentry: Talk with prudence to a beggar Of 'Potosi' and the mines!

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIX
scenes.reentry: Good night! which put the candle out?

scenes.title: Chapter XL
scenes.reentry: When I hoped I feared, Since I hoped I dared; Everywhere alone As a church remain; Spectre cannot harm, Serpent cannot charm; He deposes doom, Who hath suffered him.

scenes.title: Chapter XLI
scenes.reentry: DEED. A deed knocks first at thought, And then it knocks at will.

scenes.title: Chapter XLII
scenes.reentry: Mine enemy is growing old, -I have at last revenge.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIII
scenes.reentry: REMORSE.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIV
scenes.reentry: The body grows outside, -The more convenient way, -That if the spirit like to hide, Its temple stands alway Ajar, secure, inviting; It never did betray The soul that asked its shelter In timid honesty.

scenes.title: Chapter XLV
scenes.reentry: Undue significance a starving man attaches To food Far off; he sighs, and therefore hopeless, And therefore good.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVI
scenes.reentry: Heart not so heavy as mine, Wending late home, As it passed my window Whistled itself a tune, -A careless snatch, a ballad, A ditty of the street; Yet to my irritated ear An anodyne so sweet, It was as if a bobolink, Sauntering this way, Carolled and mused and carolled, Then bubbled slow away.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVII
scenes.reentry: I many times thought peace had come, When peace was far away; As wrecked men deem they sight the land At centre of the sea, And struggle slacker, but to prove, As hopelessly as I, How many the fictitious shores Before the harbor lie.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVIII
scenes.reentry: Unto my books so good to turn Far ends of tired days; It half endears the abstinence, And pain is missed in praise.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIX
scenes.reentry: This merit hath the worst, -It cannot be again.

scenes.title: Chapter L
scenes.reentry: HUNGER. I had been hungry all the years; My noon had come, to dine; I, trembling, drew the table near, And touched the curious wine. ' T was this on tables I had seen, When turning, hungry, lone, I looked in windows, for the wealth I could not hope to own.

scenes.title: Chapter LI
scenes.reentry: I gained it so, By climbing slow, By catching at the twigs that grow Between the bliss and me.

scenes.title: Chapter LII
scenes.reentry: To learn the transport by the pain, As blind men learn the sun; To die of thirst, suspecting That brooks in meadows run; To stay the homesick, homesick feet Upon a foreign shore Haunted by native lands, the while, And blue, beloved air -This is the sovereign anguish, This, the signal woe!

scenes.title: Chapter LIII
scenes.reentry: I years had been from home, And now, before the door, I dared not open, lest a face I never saw before Stare vacant into mine And ask my business there.

scenes.title: Chapter LIV
scenes.reentry: PRAYER. Prayer is the little implement Through which men reach Where presence is denied them.

scenes.title: Chapter LV
scenes.reentry: I know that he exists Somewhere, in silence.

scenes.title: Chapter LVI
scenes.reentry: Musicians wrestle everywhere: All day, among the crowded air, I hear the silver strife; And -- waking long before the dawn -Such transport breaks upon the town I think it that "new life!"

scenes.title: Chapter LVII
scenes.reentry: Just lost when I was saved!

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: CHOICE. Of all the souls that stand create I have elected one.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: I have no life but this, To lead it here; Nor any death, but lest Dispelled from there; Nor tie to earths to come, Nor action new, Except through this extent, The realm of you.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: Your riches taught me poverty.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: I gave myself to him, And took himself for pay.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: "GOING to him!

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: The way I read a letter 's this: 'T is first I lock the door, And push it with my fingers next, For transport it be sure.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: Wild nights!

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: AT HOME.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: Did the harebell loose her girdle To the lover bee, Would the bee the harebell hallow Much as formerly?

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: A charm invests a face Imperfectly beheld, -The lady dare not lift her veil For fear it be dispelled.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: The rose did caper on her cheek, Her bodice rose and fell, Her pretty speech, like drunken men, Did stagger pitiful.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: In lands I never saw, they say, Immortal Alps look down, Whose bonnets touch the firmament, Whose sandals touch the town, -Meek at whose everlasting feet A myriad daisies play.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: The moon is distant from the sea, And yet with amber hands She leads him, docile as a boy, Along appointed sands.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: He put the belt around my life, -I heard the buckle snap, And turned away, imperial, My lifetime folding up Deliberate, as a duke would do A kingdom's title-deed, -Henceforth a dedicated sort, A member of the cloud.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: I held a jewel in my fingers And went to sleep.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: What if I say I shall not wait?

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: Nature, the gentlest mother, Impatient of no child, The feeblest or the waywardest, -Her admonition mild In forest and the hill By traveller is heard, Restraining rampant squirrel Or too impetuous bird.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: Will there really be a morning?

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: At half-past three a single bird Unto a silent sky Propounded but a single term Of cautious melody.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: The day came slow, till five o'clock, Then sprang before the hills Like hindered rubies, or the light A sudden musket spills.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: The sun just touched the morning; The morning, happy thing, Supposed that he had come to dwell, And life would be all spring.

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: The robin is the one That interrupts the morn With hurried, few, express reports When March is scarcely on.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: From cocoon forth a butterfly As lady from her door Emerged -- a summer afternoon -Repairing everywhere, Without design, that I could trace, Except to stray abroad On miscellaneous enterprise The clovers understood.

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: Before you thought of spring, Except as a surmise, You see, God bless his suddenness, A fellow in the skies Of independent hues, A little weather-worn, Inspiriting habiliments Of indigo and brown.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: APRIL. An altered look about the hills; A Tyrian light the village fills; A wider sunrise in the dawn; A deeper twilight on the lawn; A print of a vermilion foot; A purple finger on the slope; A flippant fly upon the pane; A spider at his trade again; An added strut in chanticleer; A flower expected everywhere; An axe shrill singing in the woods; Fern-odors on untravelled roads, -All this, and more I cannot tell, A furtive look you know as well, And Nicodemus' mystery Receives its annual reply.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: "Whose are the little beds," I asked, "Which in the valleys lie?"

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: MY ROSE.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: To hear an oriole sing May be a common thing, Or only a divine.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: One of the ones that Midas touched, Who failed to touch us all, Was that confiding prodigal, The blissful oriole.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: I dreaded that first robin so, But he is mastered now, And I 'm accustomed to him grown, -He hurts a little, though.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: A route of evanescence With a revolving wheel; A resonance of emerald, A rush of cochineal; And every blossom on the bush Adjusts its tumbled head, -The mail from Tunis, probably, An easy morning's ride.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: SECRETS.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: Who robbed the woods, The trusting woods?

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: Two butterflies went out at noon And waltzed above a stream, Then stepped straight through the firmament And rested on a beam; And then together bore away Upon a shining sea, -Though never yet, in any port, Their coming mentioned be.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: I started early, took my dog, And visited the sea; The mermaids in the basement Came out to look at me, And frigates in the upper floor Extended hempen hands, Presuming me to be a mouse Aground, upon the sands.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: Arcturus is his other name, -I'd rather call him star!

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: An awful tempest mashed the air, The clouds were gaunt and few; A black, as of a spectre's cloak, Hid heaven and earth from view.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: THE SEA.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: A bird came down the walk: He did not know I saw; He bit an angle-worm in halves And ate the fellow, raw.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: A narrow fellow in the grass Occasionally rides; You may have met him, -- did you not, His notice sudden is.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: The mushroom is the elf of plants, At evening it is not; At morning in a truffled hut It stops upon a spot As if it tarried always; And yet its whole career Is shorter than a snake's delay, And fleeter than a tare. ' T is vegetation's juggler, The germ of alibi; Doth like a bubble antedate, And like a bubble hie.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: There came a wind like a bugle; It quivered through the grass, And a green chill upon the heat So ominous did pass We barred the windows and the doors As from an emerald ghost; The doom's electric moccason That very instant passed.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: A spider sewed at night Without a light Upon an arc of white.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: I know a place where summer strives With such a practised frost, She each year leads her daisies back, Recording briefly, "Lost."

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: The one that could repeat the summer day Were greater than itself, though he Minutest of mankind might be.

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: The wind tapped like a tired man, And like a host, "Come in," I boldly answered; entered then My residence within A rapid, footless guest, To offer whom a chair Were as impossible as hand A sofa to the air.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: Nature rarer uses yellow Than another hue; Saves she all of that for sunsets, -Prodigal of blue, Spending scarlet like a woman, Yellow she affords Only scantly and selectly, Like a lover's words.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXII
scenes.reentry: GOSSIP. The leaves, like women, interchange Sagacious confidence; Somewhat of nods, and somewhat of Portentous inference, The parties in both cases Enjoining secrecy, -Inviolable compact To notoriety.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIII
scenes.reentry: How happy is the little stone That rambles in the road alone, And doesn't care about careers, And exigencies never fears; Whose coat of elemental brown A passing universe put on; And independent as the sun, Associates or glows alone, Fulfilling absolute decree In casual simplicity.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIV
scenes.reentry: STORM. It sounded as if the streets were running, And then the streets stood still.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXV
scenes.reentry: THE RAT.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVI
scenes.reentry: Frequently the woods are pink, Frequently are brown; Frequently the hills undress Behind my native town.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVII
scenes.reentry: The wind begun to rock the grass With threatening tunes and low, -He flung a menace at the earth, A menace at the sky.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIX
scenes.reentry: SUNSET. Where ships of purple gently toss On seas of daffodil, Fantastic sailors mingle, And then -- the wharf is still.

scenes.title: Chapter XL
scenes.reentry: She sweeps with many-colored brooms, And leaves the shreds behind; Oh, housewife in the evening west, Come back, and dust the pond!

scenes.title: Chapter XLI
scenes.reentry: Like mighty footlights burned the red At bases of the trees, -The far theatricals of day Exhibiting to these. ' T was universe that did applaud While, chiefest of the crowd, Enabled by his royal dress, Myself distinguished God.

scenes.title: Chapter XLII
scenes.reentry: Bring me the sunset in a cup, Reckon the morning's flagons up, And say how many dew; Tell me how far the morning leaps, Tell me what time the weaver sleeps Who spun the breadths of blue!

scenes.title: Chapter XLIII
scenes.reentry: Blazing in gold and quenching in purple, Leaping like leopards to the sky, Then at the feet of the old horizon Laying her spotted face, to die; Stooping as low as the otter's window, Touching the roof and tinting the barn, Kissing her bonnet to the meadow, -And the juggler of day is gone!

scenes.title: Chapter XLIV
scenes.reentry: Farther in summer than the birds, Pathetic from the grass, A minor nation celebrates Its unobtrusive mass.

scenes.title: Chapter XLV
scenes.reentry: As imperceptibly as grief The summer lapsed away, -Too imperceptible, at last, To seem like perfidy.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVI
scenes.reentry: It can't be summer, -- that got through; It 's early yet for spring; There 's that long town of white to cross Before the blackbirds sing.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVII
scenes.reentry: The gentian weaves her fringes, The maple's loom is red.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVIII
scenes.reentry: God made a little gentian; It tried to be a rose And failed, and all the summer laughed.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIX
scenes.reentry: Besides the autumn poets sing, A few prosaic days A little this side of the snow And that side of the haze.

scenes.title: Chapter L
scenes.reentry: THE SNOW.

scenes.title: Chapter LI
scenes.reentry: No brigadier throughout the year So civic as the jay.

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: Let down the bars, O Death!

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: Going to heaven!

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: At least to pray is left, is left.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: EPITAPH.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: Morns like these we parted; Noons like these she rose, Fluttering first, then firmer, To her fair repose.

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: A death-blow is a life-blow to some Who, till they died, did not alive become; Who, had they lived, had died, but when They died, vitality begun.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: I read my sentence steadily, Reviewed it with my eyes, To see that I made no mistake In its extremest clause, -The date, and manner of the shame; And then the pious form That "God have mercy" on the soul The jury voted him.

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: I have not told my garden yet, Lest that should conquer me; I have not quite the strength now To break it to the bee.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: They dropped like flakes, they dropped like stars, Like petals from a rose, When suddenly across the June A wind with fingers goes.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: The only ghost I ever saw Was dressed in mechlin, -- so; He wore no sandal on his foot, And stepped like flakes of snow.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: Some, too fragile for winter winds, The thoughtful grave encloses, -Tenderly tucking them in from frost Before their feet are cold.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: As by the dead we love to sit, Become so wondrous dear, As for the lost we grapple, Though all the rest are here, -In broken mathematics We estimate our prize, Vast, in its fading ratio, To our penurious eyes!

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: Death sets a thing significant The eye had hurried by, Except a perished creature Entreat us tenderly To ponder little workmanships In crayon or in wool, With "This was last her fingers did," Industrious until The thimble weighed too heavy, The stitches stopped themselves, And then 't was put among the dust Upon the closet shelves.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: I went to heaven, -- 'T was a small town, Lit with a ruby, Lathed with down.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: Their height in heaven comforts not, Their glory nought to me; 'T was best imperfect, as it was; I 'm finite, I can't see.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: There is a shame of nobleness Confronting sudden pelf, -A finer shame of ecstasy Convicted of itself.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: TRIUMPH.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: Pompless no life can pass away; The lowliest career To the same pageant wends its way As that exalted here.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: I noticed people disappeared, When but a little child, -Supposed they visited remote, Or settled regions wild.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: I had no cause to be awake, My best was gone to sleep, And morn a new politeness took, And failed to wake them up, But called the others clear, And passed their curtains by.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: If anybody's friend be dead, It 's sharpest of the theme The thinking how they walked alive, At such and such a time.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: Our journey had advanced; Our feet were almost come To that odd fork in Being's road, Eternity by term.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: Ample make this bed.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: GOING. On such a night, or such a night, Would anybody care If such a little figure Slipped quiet from its chair, So quiet, oh, how quiet!

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: Essential oils are wrung: The attar from the rose Is not expressed by suns alone, It is the gift of screws.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: I lived on dread; to those who know The stimulus there is In danger, other impetus Is numb and vital-less.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: If I should die, And you should live, And time should gurgle on, And morn should beam, And noon should burn, As it has usual done; If birds should build as early, And bees as bustling go, -One might depart at option From enterprise below! 'T is sweet to know that stocks will stand When we with daisies lie, That commerce will continue, And trades as briskly fly.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: Her final summer was it, And yet we guessed it not; If tenderer industriousness Pervaded her, we thought A further force of life Developed from within, -When Death lit all the shortness up, And made the hurry plain.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: GHOSTS. One need not be a chamber to be haunted, One need not be a house; The brain has corridors surpassing Material place.

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: She died, -- this was the way she died; And when her breath was done, Took up her simple wardrobe And started for the sun.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: Wait till the majesty of Death Invests so mean a brow!

scenes.title: Chapter XXXII
scenes.reentry: GONE. Went up a year this evening!

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIII
scenes.reentry: REQUIEM.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIV
scenes.reentry: What inn is this Where for the night Peculiar traveller comes?

scenes.title: Chapter XXXV
scenes.reentry: It was not death, for I stood up, And all the dead lie down; It was not night, for all the bells Put out their tongues, for noon.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVI
scenes.reentry: I should not dare to leave my friend, Because -- because if he should die While I was gone, and I -- too late -Should reach the heart that wanted me; If I should disappoint the eyes That hunted, hunted so, to see, And could not bear to shut until They "noticed" me -- they noticed me; If I should stab the patient faith So sure I 'd come -- so sure I 'd come, It listening, listening, went to sleep Telling my tardy name, -My heart would wish it broke before, Since breaking then, since breaking then, Were useless as next morning's sun, Where midnight frosts had lain!

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVII
scenes.reentry: VOID. Great streets of silence led away To neighborhoods of pause; Here was no notice, no dissent, No universe, no laws.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIX
scenes.reentry: SAVED! Of tribulation these are they Denoted by the white; The spangled gowns, a lesser rank Of victors designate.

scenes.title: Chapter XL
scenes.reentry: I think just how my shape will rise When I shall be forgiven, Till hair and eyes and timid head Are out of sight, in heaven.

scenes.title: Chapter XLI
scenes.reentry: After a hundred years Nobody knows the place, -Agony, that enacted there, Motionless as peace.

scenes.title: Chapter XLII
scenes.reentry: Lay this laurel on the one Too intrinsic for renown.

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: T is little I could care for pearls Who own the ample sea; Or brooches, when the Emperor With rubies pelteth me; Or gold, who am the Prince of Mines; Or diamonds, when I see A diadem to fit a dome Continual crowning me.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: Superiority to fate Is difficult to learn. 'T is not conferred by any, But possible to earn A pittance at a time, Until, to her surprise, The soul with strict economy Subsists till Paradise.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: HOPE. Hope is a subtle glutton; He feeds upon the fair; And yet, inspected closely, What abstinence is there!

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: Forbidden fruit a flavor has That lawful orchards mocks; How luscious lies the pea within The pod that Duty locks!

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: Heaven is what I cannot reach!

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: A WORD. A word is dead When it is said, Some say.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: To venerate the simple days Which lead the seasons by, Needs but to remember That from you or me They may take the trifle Termed mortality!

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: It's such a little thing to weep, So short a thing to sigh; And yet by trades the size of these We men and women die!

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: Drowning is not so pitiful As the attempt to rise.

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: How still the bells in steeples stand, Till, swollen with the sky, They leap upon their silver feet In frantic melody!

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: If the foolish call them 'flowers,' Need the wiser tell?

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: Could mortal lip divine The undeveloped freight Of a delivered syllable, 'T would crumble with the weight.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: PARTING.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: We never know how high we are Till we are called to rise; And then, if we are true to plan, Our statures touch the skies.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: While I was fearing it, it came, But came with less of fear, Because that fearing it so long Had almost made it dear.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: A BOOK. There is no frigate like a book To take us lands away, Nor any coursers like a page Of prancing poetry.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: Who has not found the heaven below Will fail of it above.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: A face devoid of love or grace, A hateful, hard, successful face, A face with which a stone Would feel as thoroughly at ease As were they old acquaintances, -First time together thrown.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: I had a guinea golden; I lost it in the sand, And though the sum was simple, And pounds were in the land, Still had it such a value Unto my frugal eye, That when I could not find it I sat me down to sigh.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: From all the jails the boys and girls Ecstatically leap, -Beloved, only afternoon That prison doesn't keep.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: Few get enough, -- enough is one; To that ethereal throng Have not each one of us the right To stealthily belong?

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: Upon the gallows hung a wretch, Too sullied for the hell To which the law entitled him.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: I felt a clearing in my mind As if my brain had split; I tried to match it, seam by seam, But could not make them fit.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: The reticent volcano keeps His never slumbering plan; Confided are his projects pink To no precarious man.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: If recollecting were forgetting, Then I remember not; And if forgetting, recollecting, How near I had forgot!

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: The farthest thunder that I heard Was nearer than the sky, And rumbles still, though torrid noons Have lain their missiles by.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: On the bleakness of my lot Bloom I strove to raise.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: A door just opened on a street -I, lost, was passing by -An instant's width of warmth disclosed, And wealth, and company.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: FRIENDS.

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: FIRE. Ashes denote that fire was; Respect the grayest pile For the departed creature's sake That hovered there awhile.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: A MAN. Fate slew him, but he did not drop; She felled -- he did not fall -Impaled him on her fiercest stakes -He neutralized them all.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXII
scenes.reentry: Finite to fail, but infinite to venture.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIII
scenes.reentry: GRIEFS. I measure every grief I meet With analytic eyes; I wonder if it weighs like mine, Or has an easier size.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIV
scenes.reentry: I have a king who does not speak; So, wondering, thro' the hours meek I trudge the day away,-Half glad when it is night and sleep, If, haply, thro' a dream to peep In parlors shut by day.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXV
scenes.reentry: It dropped so low in my regard I heard it hit the ground, And go to pieces on the stones At bottom of my mind; Yet blamed the fate that fractured, less Than I reviled myself For entertaining plated wares Upon my silver shelf.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVI
scenes.reentry: To lose one's faith surpasses The loss of an estate, Because estates can be Replenished, -- faith cannot.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVII
scenes.reentry: LOST JOY.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIX
scenes.reentry: Life, and Death, and Giants Such as these, are still.

scenes.title: Chapter XL
scenes.reentry: Our lives are Swiss, -So still, so cool, Till, some odd afternoon, The Alps neglect their curtains, And we look farther on.

scenes.title: Chapter XLI
scenes.reentry: Remembrance has a rear and front, -- 'T is something like a house; It has a garret also For refuse and the mouse, Besides, the deepest cellar That ever mason hewed; Look to it, by its fathoms Ourselves be not pursued.

scenes.title: Chapter XLII
scenes.reentry: To hang our head ostensibly, And subsequent to find That such was not the posture Of our immortal mind, Affords the sly presumption That, in so dense a fuzz, You, too, take cobweb attitudes Upon a plane of gauze!

scenes.title: Chapter XLIII
scenes.reentry: The brain is wider than the sky, For, put them side by side, The one the other will include With ease, and you beside.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIV
scenes.reentry: The bone that has no marrow; What ultimate for that?

scenes.title: Chapter XLV
scenes.reentry: THE PAST.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVI
scenes.reentry: To help our bleaker parts Salubrious hours are given, Which if they do not fit for earth Drill silently for heaven.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVII
scenes.reentry: What soft, cherubic creatures These gentlewomen are!

scenes.title: Chapter XLVIII
scenes.reentry: DESIRE. Who never wanted, -- maddest joy Remains to him unknown: The banquet of abstemiousness Surpasses that of wine.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIX
scenes.reentry: It might be easier To fail with land in sight, Than gain my blue peninsula To perish of delight.

scenes.title: Chapter L
scenes.reentry: POWER. You cannot put a fire out; A thing that can ignite Can go, itself, without a fan Upon the slowest night.

scenes.title: Chapter LI
scenes.reentry: A modest lot, a fame petite, A brief campaign of sting and sweet Is plenty!

scenes.title: Chapter LII
scenes.reentry: Is bliss, then, such abyss I must not put my foot amiss For fear I spoil my shoe?

scenes.title: Chapter LIII
scenes.reentry: I stepped from plank to plank So slow and cautiously; The stars about my head I felt, About my feet the sea.

scenes.title: Chapter LIV
scenes.reentry: One day is there of the series Termed Thanksgiving day, Celebrated part at table, Part in memory.

scenes.title: Chapter LV
scenes.reentry: Softened by Time's consummate plush, How sleek the woe appears That threatened childhood's citadel And undermined the years!

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: Proud of my broken heart since thou didst break it, Proud of the pain I did not feel till thee, Proud of my night since thou with moons dost slake it, Not to partake thy passion, my humility.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: My worthiness is all my doubt, His merit all my fear, Contrasting which, my qualities Do lowlier appear; Lest I should insufficient prove For his beloved need, The chiefest apprehension Within my loving creed.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: LOVE. Love is anterior to life, Posterior to death, Initial of creation, and The exponent of breath.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: One blessing had I, than the rest So larger to my eyes That I stopped gauging, satisfied, For this enchanted size.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: When roses cease to bloom, dear, And violets are done, When bumble-bees in solemn flight Have passed beyond the sun, The hand that paused to gather Upon this summer's day Will idle lie, in Auburn, -Then take my flower, pray!

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: SONG. Summer for thee grant I may be When summer days are flown!

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: LOYALTY.

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: To lose thee, sweeter than to gain All other hearts I knew. 'T is true the drought is destitute, But then I had the dew!

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: Poor little heart!

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: There is a word Which bears a sword Can pierce an armed man.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: I've got an arrow here; Loving the hand that sent it, I the dart revere.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: He fumbles at your spirit As players at the keys Before they drop full music on; He stuns you by degrees, Prepares your brittle substance For the ethereal blow, By fainter hammers, further heard, Then nearer, then so slow Your breath has time to straighten, Your brain to bubble cool, -Deals one imperial thunderbolt That scalps your naked soul.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: Heart, we will forget him!

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: Father, I bring thee not myself, -That were the little load; I bring thee the imperial heart I had not strength to hold.

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: We outgrow love like other things And put it in the drawer, Till it an antique fashion shows Like costumes grandsires wore.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: Not with a club the heart is broken, Nor with a stone; A whip, so small you could not see it.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: WHO? My friend must be a bird, Because it flies!

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: He touched me, so I live to know That such a day, permitted so, I groped upon his breast.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: DREAMS. Let me not mar that perfect dream By an auroral stain, But so adjust my daily night That it will come again.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: I live with him, I see his face; I go no more away For visitor, or sundown; Death's single privacy, The only one forestalling mine, And that by right that he Presents a claim invisible, No wedlock granted me.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: LONGING.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: WEDDED. A solemn thing it was, I said, A woman white to be, And wear, if God should count me fit, Her hallowed mystery.

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: The springtime's pallid landscape Will glow like bright bouquet, Though drifted deep in parian The village lies to-day.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: She slept beneath a tree Remembered but by me.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: A light exists in spring Not present on the year At any other period.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: A lady red upon the hill Her annual secret keeps; A lady white within the field In placid lily sleeps!

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: TO MARCH.

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: MARCH. We like March, his shoes are purple, He is new and high; Makes he mud for dog and peddler, Makes he forest dry; Knows the adder's tongue his coming, And begets her spot.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: DAWN. Not knowing when the dawn will come I open every door; Or has it feathers like a bird, Or billows like a shore?

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: A murmur in the trees to note, Not loud enough for wind; A star not far enough to seek, Nor near enough to find; A long, long yellow on the lawn, A hubbub as of feet; Not audible, as ours to us, But dapperer, more sweet; A hurrying home of little men To houses unperceived, -All this, and more, if I should tell, Would never be believed.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: Morning is the place for dew, Corn is made at noon, After dinner light for flowers, Dukes for setting sun!

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: To my quick ear the leaves conferred; The bushes they were bells; I could not find a privacy From Nature's sentinels.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: A ROSE. A sepal, petal, and a thorn Upon a common summer's morn, A flash of dew, a bee or two, A breeze A caper in the trees, -And I'm a rose!

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: High from the earth I heard a bird; He trod upon the trees As he esteemed them trifles, And then he spied a breeze, And situated softly Upon a pile of wind Which in a perturbation Nature had left behind.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: COBWEBS.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: A WELL. What mystery pervades a well!

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: To make a prairie it takes a clover and one bee, -One clover, and a bee, And revery.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: THE WIND.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: A dew sufficed itself And satisfied a leaf, And felt, 'how vast a destiny!

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: His bill an auger is, His head, a cap and frill.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: A SNAKE.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: Could I but ride indefinite, As doth the meadow-bee, And visit only where I liked, And no man visit me, And flirt all day with buttercups, And marry whom I may, And dwell a little everywhere, Or better, run away With no police to follow, Or chase me if I do, Till I should jump peninsulas To get away from you, -I said, but just to be a bee Upon a raft of air, And row in nowhere all day long, And anchor off the bar,-What liberty!

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: THE MOON.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: THE BAT.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: You've seen balloons set, haven't you?

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: EVENING.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: COCOON. Drab habitation of whom?

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: SUNSET. A sloop of amber slips away Upon an ether sea, And wrecks in peace a purple tar, The son of ecstasy.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: AURORA. Of bronze and blaze The north, to-night!

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: How the old mountains drip with sunset, And the brake of dun!

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: The murmuring of bees has ceased; But murmuring of some Posterior, prophetic, Has simultaneous come, -The lower metres of the year, When nature's laugh is done, -The Revelations of the book Whose Genesis is June.

scenes.title: Chapter I
scenes.reentry: This world is not conclusion; A sequel stands beyond, Invisible, as music, But positive, as sound.

scenes.title: Chapter II
scenes.reentry: We learn in the retreating How vast an one Was recently among us.

scenes.title: Chapter III
scenes.reentry: They say that 'time assuages,' -Time never did assuage; An actual suffering strengthens, As sinews do, with age.

scenes.title: Chapter IV
scenes.reentry: We cover thee, sweet face.

scenes.title: Chapter V
scenes.reentry: ENDING. That is solemn we have ended, -Be it but a play, Or a glee among the garrets, Or a holiday, Or a leaving home; or later, Parting with a world We have understood, for better Still it be unfurled.

scenes.title: Chapter VI
scenes.reentry: The stimulus, beyond the grave His countenance to see, Supports me like imperial drams Afforded royally.

scenes.title: Chapter VII
scenes.reentry: Given in marriage unto thee, Oh, thou celestial host!

scenes.title: Chapter VIII
scenes.reentry: That such have died enables us The tranquiller to die; That such have lived, certificate For immortality.

scenes.title: Chapter IX
scenes.reentry: They won't frown always, -- some sweet day When I forget to tease, They'll recollect how cold I looked, And how I just said 'please.'

scenes.title: Chapter X
scenes.reentry: It is an honorable thought, And makes one lift one's hat, As one encountered gentlefolk Upon a daily street, That we've immortal place, Though pyramids decay, And kingdoms, like the orchard, Flit russetly away.

scenes.title: Chapter XI
scenes.reentry: The distance that the dead have gone Does not at first appear; Their coming back seems possible For many an ardent year.

scenes.title: Chapter XII
scenes.reentry: How dare the robins sing, When men and women hear Who since they went to their account Have settled with the year! -Paid all that life had earned In one consummate bill, And now, what life or death can do Is immaterial.

scenes.title: Chapter XIII
scenes.reentry: DEATH. Death is like the insect Menacing the tree, Competent to kill it, But decoyed may be.

scenes.title: Chapter XIV
scenes.reentry: T is sunrise, little maid, hast thou No station in the day? 'T was not thy wont to hinder so, -Retrieve thine industry. ' T is noon, my little maid, alas!

scenes.title: Chapter XV
scenes.reentry: Each that we lose takes part of us; A crescent still abides, Which like the moon, some turbid night, Is summoned by the tides.

scenes.title: Chapter XVI
scenes.reentry: Not any higher stands the grave For heroes than for men; Not any nearer for the child Than numb three-score and ten.

scenes.title: Chapter XVII
scenes.reentry: ASLEEP. As far from pity as complaint, As cool to speech as stone, As numb to revelation As if my trade were bone.

scenes.title: Chapter XVIII
scenes.reentry: T is whiter than an Indian pipe, 'T is dimmer than a lace; No stature has it, like a fog, When you approach the place.

scenes.title: Chapter XIX
scenes.reentry: She laid her docile crescent down, And this mechanic stone Still states, to dates that have forgot, The news that she is gone.

scenes.title: Chapter XX
scenes.reentry: Bless God, he went as soldiers, His musket on his breast; Grant, God, he charge the bravest Of all the martial blest.

scenes.title: Chapter XXI
scenes.reentry: Immortal is an ample word When what we need is by, But when it leaves us for a time, 'T is a necessity.

scenes.title: Chapter XXII
scenes.reentry: Where every bird is bold to go, And bees abashless play, The foreigner before he knocks Must thrust the tears away.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIII
scenes.reentry: The grave my little cottage is, Where, keeping house for thee, I make my parlor orderly, And lay the marble tea, For two divided, briefly, A cycle, it may be, Till everlasting life unite In strong society.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIV
scenes.reentry: This was in the white of the year, That was in the green, Drifts were as difficult then to think As daisies now to be seen.

scenes.title: Chapter XXV
scenes.reentry: Sweet hours have perished here; This is a mighty room; Within its precincts hopes have played, -Now shadows in the tomb.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVI
scenes.reentry: Me! Come!

scenes.title: Chapter XXVII
scenes.reentry: From us she wandered now a year, Her tarrying unknown; If wilderness prevent her feet, Or that ethereal zone No eye hath seen and lived, We ignorant must be.

scenes.title: Chapter XXVIII
scenes.reentry: I wish I knew that woman's name, So, when she comes this way, To hold my life, and hold my ears, For fear I hear her say She's 'sorry I am dead,' again, Just when the grave and I Have sobbed ourselves almost to sleep, -Our only lullaby.

scenes.title: Chapter XXIX
scenes.reentry: Bereaved of all, I went abroad, No less bereaved to be Upon a new peninsula, -The grave preceded me, Obtained my lodgings ere myself, And when I sought my bed, The grave it was, reposed upon The pillow for my head.

scenes.title: Chapter XXX
scenes.reentry: I felt a funeral in my brain, And mourners, to and fro, Kept treading, treading, till it seemed That sense was breaking through.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXI
scenes.reentry: I meant to find her when I came; Death had the same design; But the success was his, it seems, And the discomfit mine.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXII
scenes.reentry: WAITING.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIII
scenes.reentry: A sickness of this world it most occasions When best men die; A wishfulness their far condition To occupy.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIV
scenes.reentry: Superfluous were the sun When excellence is dead; He were superfluous every day, For every day is said That syllable whose faith Just saves it from despair, And whose 'I'll meet you' hesitates If love inquire, 'Where?'

scenes.title: Chapter XXXV
scenes.reentry: So proud she was to die It made us all ashamed That what we cherished, so unknown To her desire seemed.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVI
scenes.reentry: Tie the strings to my life, my Lord, Then I am ready to go!

scenes.title: Chapter XXXVII
scenes.reentry: The dying need but little, dear, -A glass of water's all, A flower's unobtrusive face To punctuate the wall, A fan, perhaps, a friend's regret, And certainly that one No color in the rainbow Perceives when you are gone.

scenes.title: Chapter XXXIX
scenes.reentry: The soul should always stand ajar, That if the heaven inquire, He will not be obliged to wait, Or shy of troubling her.

scenes.title: Chapter XL
scenes.reentry: Three weeks passed since I had seen her, -Some disease had vexed; 'T was with text and village singing I beheld her next, And a company -- our pleasure To discourse alone; Gracious now to me as any, Gracious unto none.

scenes.title: Chapter XLI
scenes.reentry: I breathed enough to learn the trick, And now, removed from air, I simulate the breath so well, That one, to be quite sure The lungs are stirless, must descend Among the cunning cells, And touch the pantomime himself.

scenes.title: Chapter XLII
scenes.reentry: I wonder if the sepulchre Is not a lonesome way, When men and boys, and larks and June Go down the fields to hay!

scenes.title: Chapter XLIII
scenes.reentry: If tolling bell I ask the cause. 'A soul has gone to God,' I'm answered in a lonesome tone; Is heaven then so sad?

scenes.title: Chapter XLIV
scenes.reentry: If I may have it when it's dead I will contented be; If just as soon as breath is out It shall belong to me, Until they lock it in the grave, 'T is bliss I cannot weigh, For though they lock thee in the grave, Myself can hold the key.

scenes.title: Chapter XLV
scenes.reentry: Before the ice is in the pools, Before the skaters go, Or any cheek at nightfall Is tarnished by the snow, Before the fields have finished, Before the Christmas tree, Wonder upon wonder Will arrive to me!

scenes.title: Chapter XLVI
scenes.reentry: DYING. I heard a fly buzz when I died; The stillness round my form Was like the stillness in the air Between the heaves of storm.

scenes.title: Chapter XLVII
scenes.reentry: Adrift! A little boat adrift!

scenes.title: Chapter XLVIII
scenes.reentry: There's been a death in the opposite house As lately as to-day.

scenes.title: Chapter XLIX
scenes.reentry: We never know we go, -- when we are going We jest and shut the door; Fate following behind us bolts it, And we accost no more.

scenes.title: Chapter L
scenes.reentry: It struck me every day The lightning was as new As if the cloud that instant slit And let the fire through.

scenes.title: Chapter LI
scenes.reentry: Water is taught by thirst; Land, by the oceans passed; Transport, by throe; Peace, by its battles told; Love, by memorial mould; Birds, by the snow.

scenes.title: Chapter LII
scenes.reentry: THIRST. We thirst at first, -- 't is Nature's act; And later, when we die, A little water supplicate Of fingers going by.

scenes.title: Chapter LIII
scenes.reentry: A clock stopped -- not the mantel's; Geneva's farthest skill Can't put the puppet bowing That just now dangled still.

scenes.title: Chapter LIV
scenes.reentry: All overgrown by cunning moss, All interspersed with weed, The little cage of 'Currer Bell,' In quiet Haworth laid.

scenes.title: Chapter LV
scenes.reentry: A toad can die of light!

scenes.title: Chapter LVI
scenes.reentry: Far from love the Heavenly Father Leads the chosen child; Oftener through realm of briar Than the meadow mild, Oftener by the claw of dragon Than the hand of friend, Guides the little one predestined To the native land.

scenes.title: Chapter LVII
scenes.reentry: A long, long sleep, a famous sleep That makes no show for dawn By stretch of limb or stir of lid, -An independent one.

scenes.title: Chapter LVIII
scenes.reentry: T was just this time last year I died.

scenes.title: Chapter LIX
scenes.reentry: On this wondrous sea, Sailing silently, Ho! pilot, ho!

breaths.text: Success is counted sweetest By those who ne'er succeed.
To comprehend a nectar Requires sorest need.

Not one of all the purple host Who took the flag to-day Can tell the definition, So clear, of victory, As he, defeated, dying, On whose forbidden ear The distant strains of triumph Break, agonized and clear!
Our share of night to bear, Our share of morning, Our blank in bliss to fill, Our blank in scorning.
Here a star, and there a star, Some lose their way.
Here a mist, and there a mist, Afterwards -- day!
Soul, wilt thou toss again?
By just such a hazard Hundreds have lost, indeed, But tens have won an all.
Angels' breathless ballot Lingers to record thee; Imps in eager caucus Raffle for my soul.
T is so much joy! 'T is so much joy!
If I should fail, what poverty!
And yet, as poor as I Have ventured all upon a throw; Have gained!
Yes! Hesitated so This side the victory!
Life is but life, and death but death!
Bliss is but bliss, and breath but breath!
And if, indeed, I fail, At least to know the worst is sweet.
Defeat means nothing but defeat, No drearier can prevail!
And if I gain, -- oh, gun at sea, Oh, bells that in the steeples be, At first repeat it slow!
For heaven is a different thing Conjectured, and waked sudden in, And might o'erwhelm me so!
Glee! The great storm is over!
Four have recovered the land; Forty gone down together Into the boiling sand.
Ring, for the scant salvation!
Toll, for the bonnie souls, -Neighbor and friend and bridegroom, Spinning upon the shoals!
How they will tell the shipwreck When winter shakes the door, Till the children ask, "But the forty?
Did they come back no more?"
Then a silence suffuses the story, And a softness the teller's eye; And the children no further question, And only the waves reply.
If I can stop one heart from breaking, I shall not live in vain; If I can ease one life the aching, Or cool one pain, Or help one fainting robin Unto his nest again, I shall not live in vain.
ALMOST! Within my reach!
I could have touched!
I might have chanced that way!
Soft sauntered through the village, Sauntered as soft away!
So unsuspected violets Within the fields lie low, Too late for striving fingers That passed, an hour ago.
A wounded deer leaps highest, I've heard the hunter tell; 'T is but the ecstasy of death, And then the brake is still.
The smitten rock that gushes, The trampled steel that springs; A cheek is always redder Just where the hectic stings!
Mirth is the mail of anguish, In which it cautions arm, Lest anybody spy the blood And "You're hurt" exclaim!

The heart asks pleasure first, And then, excuse from pain; And then, those little anodynes That deaden suffering; And then, to go to sleep; And then, if it should be The will of its Inquisitor, The liberty to die.

A precious, mouldering pleasure 't is To meet an antique book, In just the dress his century wore; A privilege, I think, His venerable hand to take, And warming in our own, A passage back, or two, to make To times when he was young.
His quaint opinions to inspect, His knowledge to unfold On what concerns our mutual mind, The literature of old; What interested scholars most, What competitions ran When Plato was a certainty.
And Sophocles a man;
When Sappho was a living girl, And Beatrice wore The gown that Dante deified.
Facts, centuries before,
He traverses familiar, As one should come to town And tell you all your dreams were true; He lived where dreams were sown.
His presence is enchantment, You beg him not to go; Old volumes shake their vellum heads And tantalize, just so.
Much madness is divinest sense To a discerning eye; Much sense the starkest madness. 'T is the majority In this, as all, prevails.
Assent, and you are sane; Demur, -- you're straightway dangerous, And handled with a chain.
I asked no other thing, No other was denied.
I offered Being for it; The mighty merchant smiled.
Brazil? He twirled a button, Without a glance my way: "But, madam, is there nothing else That we can show to-day?"
The soul selects her own society, Then shuts the door; On her divine majority Obtrude no more.
Unmoved, she notes the chariot's pausing At her low gate; Unmoved, an emperor is kneeling Upon her mat.
I've known her from an ample nation Choose one; Then close the valves of her attention Like stone.
Some things that fly there be, -Birds, hours, the bumble-bee: Of these no elegy.
Some things that stay there be, -Grief, hills, eternity: Nor this behooveth me.
There are, that resting, rise.
Can I expound the skies?
How still the riddle lies!

I know some lonely houses off the road A robber 'd like the look of, -Wooden barred, And windows hanging low, Inviting to A portico, Where two could creep: One hand the tools, The other peep To make sure all's asleep.
Old-fashioned eyes, Not easy to surprise!
How orderly the kitchen 'd look by night, With just a clock, -But they could gag the tick, And mice won't bark; And so the walls don't tell, None will.
A pair of spectacles ajar just stir -An almanac's aware.
Was it the mat winked, Or a nervous star?
The moon slides down the stair To see who's there.
There's plunder, -- where?
Tankard, or spoon, Earring, or stone, A watch, some ancient brooch To match the grandmamma, Staid sleeping there.
Day rattles, too, Stealth's slow; The sun has got as far As the third sycamore.
Screams chanticleer, "Who's there?"
And echoes, trains away, Sneer -- "Where?"
While the old couple, just astir, Fancy the sunrise left the door ajar!
To fight aloud is very brave, But gallanter, I know, Who charge within the bosom, The cavalry of woe.
Who win, and nations do not see, Who fall, and none observe, Whose dying eyes no country Regards with patriot love.
We trust, in plumed procession, For such the angels go, Rank after rank, with even feet And uniforms of snow.

DAWN. When night is almost done, And sunrise grows so near That we can touch the spaces, It 's time to smooth the hair And get the dimples ready, And wonder we could care For that old faded midnight That frightened but an hour.
Read, sweet, how others strove, Till we are stouter; What they renounced, Till we are less afraid; How many times they bore The faithful witness, Till we are helped, As if a kingdom cared!
Read then of faith That shone above the fagot; Clear strains of hymn The river could not drown; Brave names of men And celestial women, Passed out of record Into renown!
Pain has an element of blank; It cannot recollect When it began, or if there were A day when it was not.
It has no future but itself, Its infinite realms contain Its past, enlightened to perceive New periods of pain.
I taste a liquor never brewed, From tankards scooped in pearl; Not all the vats upon the Rhine Yield such an alcohol!
Inebriate of air am I, And debauchee of dew, Reeling, through endless summer days, From inns of molten blue.
When landlords turn the drunken bee Out of the foxglove's door, When butterflies renounce their drams, I shall but drink the more!
Till seraphs swing their snowy hats, And saints to windows run, To see the little tippler Leaning against the sun!
A BOOK. He ate and drank the precious words, His spirit grew robust; He knew no more that he was poor, Nor that his frame was dust.
He danced along the dingy days, And this bequest of wings Was but a book.
What liberty A loosened spirit brings!
I had no time to hate, because The grave would hinder me, And life was not so ample I Could finish enmity.
Nor had I time to love; but since Some industry must be, The little toil of love, I thought, Was large enough for me.

T was such a little, little boat That toddled down the bay! 'T was such a gallant, gallant sea That beckoned it away! ' T was such a greedy, greedy wave That licked it from the coast; Nor ever guessed the stately sails My little craft was lost!

Whether my bark went down at sea, Whether she met with gales, Whether to isles enchanted She bent her docile sails; By what mystic mooring She is held to-day, -This is the errand of the eye Out upon the bay.
Belshazzar had a letter, -He never had but one; Belshazzar's correspondent Concluded and begun In that immortal copy The conscience of us all Can read without its glasses On revelation's wall.

The brain within its groove Runs evenly and true; But let a splinter swerve, 'T were easier for you To put the water back When floods have slit the hills, And scooped a turnpike for themselves, And blotted out the mills!
MINE. Mine by the right of the white election!
Mine by the royal seal!
Mine by the sign in the scarlet prison Bars cannot conceal!
Mine, here in vision and in veto!
Mine, by the grave's repeal Titled, confirmed, -- delirious charter!
Mine, while the ages steal!
BEQUEST.

You left me, sweet, two legacies, -A legacy of love A Heavenly Father would content, Had He the offer of; You left me boundaries of pain Capacious as the sea, Between eternity and time, Your consciousness and me.
Alter? When the hills do.
Falter? When the sun Question if his glory Be the perfect one.
Surfeit?
When the daffodil Doth of the dew: Even as herself, O friend!
I will of you!
Elysium is as far as to The very nearest room, If in that room a friend await Felicity or doom.
What fortitude the soul contains, That it can so endure The accent of a coming foot, The opening of a door!
Doubt me, my dim companion!
Why, God would be content With but a fraction of the love Poured thee without a stint.
The whole of me, forever, What more the woman can, -Say quick, that I may dower thee With last delight I own!

It cannot be my spirit, For that was thine before; I ceded all of dust I knew, -What opulence the more Had I, a humble maiden, Whose farthest of degree Was that she might, Some distant heaven, Dwell timidly with thee!
If you were coming in the fall, I'd brush the summer by With half a smile and half a spurn, As housewives do a fly.
